objections.C_sol: Malaysian paip can denote the pipe more broadly, while paip air or kepala paip may identify the water-control fixture more precisely.
Indonesian wastafel commonly suggests a bathroom washbasin, while a kitchen sink may be called bak cuci piring.

objections.B_luna: Malaysian penyedut hampagas is an ordinary competing term, so pembersih vakum may not be the clearest practical preference.
objections.C_sol: Malaysian learners may more ordinarily encounter vakum or penyedut hampagas than pembersih vakum.

objections.B_luna: Pembayaran and bayaran overlap substantially in ordinary usage, so the contrast should not imply strict exclusivity.
Both languages also use the other form, so the card may overstate a strict national split.
Malay menjemput can also mean picking someone up, while mengundang remains possible in Malay.
objections.C_sol: Malaysian menjemput can also mean to pick someone up, so context is needed to preserve the intended invitation sense.

objections.B_luna: Malay also commonly uses berkunjung, while melawat can carry a more specific visiting-someone nuance in some contexts.
Malay also uses persimpangan, especially in more formal or compound descriptions.
objections.C_sol: Malaysian simpang may denote a turn or branching junction rather than an intersection specifically; persimpangan is a competing precise form.

objections.B_luna: Indonesian batas waktu is a common competing form, and tenggat waktu may sound formal or less idiomatic to learners.
Malaysian speakers commonly use straw, so penyedut minuman may sound formal or less everyday.
objections.C_sol: Malaysian speakers commonly use “straw,” so “penyedut minuman” may sound formal or descriptive rather than like the ordinary default.

objections.B_luna: Indonesian technology users commonly say file, while berkas can sound formal or suggest a dossier.
objections.C_sol: Indonesian commonly uses “file” for a digital file, while “berkas” can suggest a document or dossier and may not match the claimed everyday contrast.

objections.B_luna: Malaysian printer is also an ordinary competing form, so pencetak may overstate the national contrast.
objections.C_sol: Malaysian also commonly uses “printer,” so “pencetak” may overstate the everyday national contrast.

objections.B_luna: Malaysian pemacu USB may be more immediately ordinary than pemacu kilat for this device.
objections.C_sol: Malaysian commonly uses “pendrive” or “pemacu pena,” making “pemacu kilat” potentially unrepresentative as the practical answer.
Indonesian everyday speech often uses “download,” so “mengunduh” may imply a stronger practical preference than warranted.
Indonesian everyday speech often uses “upload,” so “mengunggah” may imply a stronger practical preference than warranted.

objections.B_luna: Malaysian hamil is also an ordinary competing form alongside mengandung.
objections.C_sol: “Hamil” is also ordinary Malaysian, while Indonesian also uses “mengandung,” so the card overstates a national lexical contrast.
Indonesian wajan and Malaysian kuali can denote wok-like or broader cooking pans rather than specifically a shallow frying pan; Malaysian kuali leper may be more precise.

objections.B_luna: Malay also uses broader beg forms, so beg pakaian may not always specifically imply a suitcase.
Malaysian also uses sumpit for chopsticks, while penyepit makanan can sound descriptive or refer to food tongs.
objections.C_sol: Malaysian penyepit makanan can sound like a generic food-gripping utensil, while chopstick is common in everyday Malaysian usage.

objections.B_luna: Malay latihan alone can mean training generally; latihan vokasional would more precisely convey vocational training.
objections.C_sol: Both pelatihan and latihan mean training broadly; Indonesian pelatihan vokasional/kejuruan and Malaysian latihan vokasional better preserve the cue's job-specific sense.
Malay ketawa is relatively colloquial, while tertawa also occurs as a more formal Malaysian form.
Malaysian balutan or pembalut may compete with the more explicitly descriptive pembalut luka.
Malaysian also commonly uses pijama, so baju tidur is not an exclusive national preference.
Indonesian speakers commonly use database, which may make basis data too formal for an ordinary-preference card.

objections.B_luna: Indonesian users commonly say spreadsheet, and Malaysian users may also use spreadsheet, so the localized forms may sound formal or less ordinary.
objections.C_sol: Spreadsheet is a common competing loan in both languages, while lembar bentang and hamparan elektronik may chiefly be formal terminology.

limitations: The benchmark deliberately includes every known unsafe historical ACCEPT; its risk prevalence is not a population estimate.
Variant A reuses archived Luna production decisions and incurs no new benchmark call. Its historical prompts and batching differ from variants B/C.
The revised contract was specified after the failure classes were known; batch-separated results are descriptive validation, not a blind prospective trial.
Random sample outcomes depend on the fixed hash seed and this small enriched set.
